'''Igor Ivanovich Akimushkin''' ({{langx|ru|link=no|Игорь Иванович Акимушкин}}) (May 1, 1929 – 1993) was a Soviet [[zoologist]] and writer.

Born in Moscow, he graduated the biological faculty of [[Moscow State University]] in 1952.
His first books, ''Tracks of beast you never met'' and ''Following the Legends'', were published in 1961.{{Citation needed|date=October 2017}}

Igor Akimushkin wrote a large number of popular science books and made a significant contribution to science and made some discoveries by exploring the marine life. Most of his works were translated to other languages. The [[squid]] ''[[Cycloteuthis akimushkini]]'' was named in honour of Igor Akimushkin in 1968 by fellow zoologist [[Filippova]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tmbl.gu.se/libdb/taxon/personetymol/index.htm|title=BEMON|publisher=|access-date=July 5, 2007|archive-date=May 16, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110516084304/http://www.tmbl.gu.se/libdb/taxon/personetymol/index.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

His most well known work is the six volume ''World of Animals''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://healthymax.org/who-you-are-igor-akimushkin-birthday-great-popularizer/|title=Who you are - Igor Akimushkin? Birthday great popularizer — HealthyMax|date=2017-01-27|work=HealthyMax|access-date=2017-10-03|language=en-US|archive-date=October 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171003225155/http://healthymax.org/who-you-are-igor-akimushkin-birthday-great-popularizer/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He worked at the [[Shirshov Institute of Oceanology|Shirshov Institute of Oceanology, Russian Academy of Sciences]].
